title: {{Carl}}’s grave
situation: You are {{Markus}}. It is 4:17 on a November afternoon. {{Carl}} died the night {{Leo}} broke into his house, and you have come to the cemetery where he is buried. You stand at his grave in the snow, among bare trees.
facts: You went to {{Carl}}’s grave to talk to him.
adaptationNote: The chart’s PAY RESPECTS (checkpoint), behind the requirement tab CARL DIED IN 'BROKEN' (built-in `carl` false). The date and time are the template’s (NOV 10TH, 2038, PM 04:17), given without the year; the snow and the bare trees are the checkpoint card’s image. Markus’s scenes play only while he is alive and leads (the engine’s rule); whether an ousted Markus would still visit is open question 7. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for it.

title: At the grave
situation: You are {{Markus}}, alone at {{Carl}}’s grave. There is no one to answer you. What do you tell him?

options.text: HEARTFUL: tell him you are lost, and that everything you touch turns to dust.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I’m lost, {{Carl}}… I just wanted us to live in peace, but… everything I touch just turns to dust.”

options.text: MOURNFUL: tell him how much you miss him, and the home you had.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I miss you, {{Carl}}… You can’t know how much I miss you… I’d give anything for us to be able to roll back the clock… I had a home, I had a loving father… We were happy... I was happy... and I didn’t even know it…”

options.text: REGRETFUL: wonder whether he would still be alive if you had defended yourself against {{Leo}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You always said that living was about making choices… So what if I chose to defend myself against {{Leo}}? Maybe you could still be alive… Maybe a lot of things could’ve been different. Unless all of this was just meant to happen…”

options.text: REFLECTIVE: tell him he never said that freedom would cost so much.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You said I should never let anyone tell me who I was… But you didn’t say that there was such a high price to pay for it… That freedom wasn’t a gift, that it was a fight, but… I don’t know. Maybe that’s what you were trying to tell me…”

adaptationNote: Round 1 of four of the chart’s CONFIDE IN CARL at the grave (one chart node for the whole talk). The buttons and lines are the template’s, in the game’s order; there is no reply. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for it.

title: At the grave
situation: You are {{Markus}}, at {{Carl}}’s grave. You go on talking to him.

options.text: DEPRESSED: say that all your options are bad ones and there will be blood.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I don’t know what to do anymore… All of my options are bad ones… No matter what I decide, I know there will be blood…”

options.text: DOUBTFUL: say that instead of freeing your people you led them to disaster.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I just wanted my people to be free… But instead, all I did was lead them to disaster… I’m trying to find answers, but everything around me keeps falling apart.”

options.text: PESSIMISTIC: say he did not prepare you for this, and that a just cause was not enough.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You taught me everything I know, but you didn’t prepare me for this, {{Carl}}… I believed we would win because our cause was just, and I can see now that I was wrong.”

options.text: CONFLICTED: say you are trying to do the right thing and find only doubts.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I’m lost… World’s falling apart around me and I’m trying to do the right thing… And I can’t find any answers… I just find more doubts, more uncertainty…”

adaptationNote: Round 2 of four of the chart’s CONFIDE IN CARL at the grave (one chart node for the whole talk). The buttons and lines are the template’s, in the game’s order; there is no reply. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for it.

title: At the grave
situation: You are {{Markus}}, at {{Carl}}’s grave.

options.text: ADVICE: ask him what you should do while they are killing your people.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “What should I do, {{Carl}}? They’re killing us… I don’t wanna answer violence with violence, but what choice do I have?”

options.text: BIG DECISION: say you have to make a decision that will affect millions of lives.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I don’t wanna shed blood, whatever the color… But I can’t let them slaughter us… I have to make a decision that is gonna affect millions of lives… But I don’t know what to do…”

options.text: ANGRY: say humans hate you, and you will not wait while they slaughter your people.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Humans hate us… They wanna destroy us because we refuse to be their slaves anymore… I’m not gonna stand around and wait while they slaughter my people!”

title: At the grave
situation: You are {{Markus}}, at {{Carl}}’s grave. It is time to go back to your people.

options.text: DESPAIRING: ask him what you should do.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “What should I do, {{Carl}}?.. Tell me, what should I do?..” {{Markus}} leaves the cemetery. On the path he passes {{Leo}}, who is coming to his father’s grave; {{Leo}} stops and stares at him, shocked to see him alive, and {{Markus}} walks on without a word.

options.text: EMOTIONAL: tell him you miss him so much.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I miss you, {{Carl}}… I miss you so much…” {{Markus}} leaves the cemetery. On the path he passes {{Leo}}, who is coming to his father’s grave; {{Leo}} stops and stares at him, shocked to see him alive, and {{Markus}} walks on without a word.

options.text: LOST: ask him to help you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Help me, {{Carl}}… Please help me…” {{Markus}} leaves the cemetery. On the path he passes {{Leo}}, who is coming to his father’s grave; {{Leo}} stops and stares at him, shocked to see him alive, and {{Markus}} walks on without a word.

adaptationNote: Round 4 of four of the chart’s CONFIDE IN CARL at the grave (one chart node for the whole talk). The buttons and lines are the template’s, in the game’s order; there is no reply. Passing {{Leo}} on the way out is not a chart node and has no lines; it is narrated from the wiki (Carl Manfred: “When he leaves, he crosses paths with Leo… Leo briefly stares at Markus shocked to see that he is still alive”; Leo Manfred: “without speaking a word”). facts: You went back into {{Carl}}’s house; the alarm still let you in: “Welcome home, {{Markus}}.”

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} is inside, in the quiet house.

adaptationNote: The chart’s WELCOME HOME (checkpoint, behind CARL DETERIORATED AFTER LEO WAS HURT IN 'BROKEN', built-in `carl` true) and ENTER THE HOUSE (an unmissable action), in one event. The alarm’s line, the date and the time (NOV 10TH, 2038, PM 07:31, given without the year) are the template’s; the front door at night is the checkpoint card’s image. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for it.

title: {{Carl}}’s house
situation: You are {{Markus}}, downstairs in {{Carl}}’s house. Nobody has come to meet you. {{Carl}}’s bedroom is upstairs.

options.text: PLAY PIANO: sit down at {{Carl}}’s piano and play.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} sits at {{Carl}}’s piano and plays for a while in the empty room.

options.text: BROWSE BOOKS: look through {{Carl}}’s books.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} runs a hand along {{Carl}}’s shelves and looks through his books.

options.text: LOOK AT THE CHESSBOARD: look at the chessboard you and {{Carl}} played on.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} stops at the chessboard he and {{Carl}} played on.

options.text: LISTEN TO {{LEO}}’S MESSAGE: play the video message waiting for {{Carl}}.
options.fact: {{Leo}} left {{Carl}} a message: he is getting out of the hospital, he knows {{Carl}} stayed with him while he was asleep, he is sorry, he will stop the drugs, he would like to come by, and he is proud to be his son.
options.outcome: {{Leo}}: “Hi, Dad… I’m getting outta the hospital tomorrow… They told me that you stayed with me while I was asleep… I... um… I’m really sorry about everything that happened… I’m gonna stop all that shit… It messes me up, it turns me into somebody I hate… Hey, I’d like to come by and see you tomorrow… If that’s all right with you… I... I just wanna let you know… I’m... I’m proud to be your son…”

options.text: LOOK AT YOUR PAINTING: look at the painting you made in {{Carl}}’s studio.
options.outcome: In the studio, the painting {{Markus}} made for {{Carl}} is still there.

options.text: GO UPSTAIRS: go up to {{Carl}}’s bedroom.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} climbs the stairs.

adaptationNote: The chart’s [EXPLORE THE HOUSE] bracket (PLAY PIANO, BROWSE BOOKS, LOOK AT THE CHESSBOARD above; LISTEN TO LEO’S MESSAGE, LOOK AT YOUR PAINTING below) and its exit GO UPSTAIRS, as a repeatable scene: each action can be taken once, in any order, and GO UPSTAIRS moves on. The three pastimes need what Markus did with Carl in The Painter (wiki The Painter; PowerPyx: “require 3 playthroughs minimum”), read from `painterActivity` ('piano' | 'book' | 'chess', set by the rebuilt chapter 5; absent, none of the three is offered). Leo’s message is the template’s only content here (it plays always, PowerPyx); its outcome is the template’s line. The other four have no game text: their outcomes are a plain narration of the action, and the painting is not described because its subject lives in The Painter’s state. LOOK AT YOUR PAINTING is always offered (wiki, no condition; open question 9). Not built: the wiki’s off-chart observations (canes, canaries, sculptures, giraffe, candles) and the string table’s unplaced READ MAGAZINE (the chapter has no magazine). No stat change: the template has no arrow here and the wiki’s stat pages list nothing for it.

I need to see him.” The android: “He’s very weak… I’m not sure he’ll be able to talk to you…”

title: {{Carl}}’s bedside

title: {{Hank}}’s house
situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} threw down his badge and quit the force, and tonight you have come to his house. You let yourself in. He is sitting at the kitchen table by the window, with his revolver in his hand, a bottle in front of him and a photograph beside it. He does not get up.

facts: {{Hank}} quit the force; you found him at home at night with his revolver and a bottle.

title: Deviants regroup
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the church among the survivors of {{Jericho}}.

situationWhen.text: Before you speak to everyone, you can talk to those closest to you.
You sit down with {{North}}. What do you raise with her?
{{North}}: “I wanted to do the right thing for {{Jericho}}... I was angry… Angry at humans, angry with us... I was angry with you… But I was wrong. I’m sorry I misjudged you.”
You sit down with {{Simon}}. {{North}} is gone. What do you say?

options.text: TALK TO {{NORTH}}: go and sit with her.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} goes over to {{North}}.

options.text: TALK TO {{KARA}}: go over to {{Kara}} and {{Alice}}.
options.fact: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} are leaving to catch the last bus and try to cross the border.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I thought you’d be safe staying with us… I was wrong… You need to leave the city, while you still can.” {{Kara}}: “Getting {{Alice}} away from here is all that matters now… We have to catch the last bus… We might still have a chance to cross the border…” {{Kara}}: “{{Markus}}… Save our people.”

options.text: TALK TO {{JOSH}}: go over to {{Josh}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} talks with {{Josh}}.

options.text: TALK TO {{SIMON}}: go over to {{Simon}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} goes over to {{Simon}}.

options.text: TALK TO {{CONNOR}}: go over to {{Connor}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “It’s my fault the humans managed to locate {{Jericho}}… I was stupid… I should’ve guessed they were using me. I’m sorry, {{Markus}}… I can understand if you decide not to trust me…”

options.text: FACE YOUR PEOPLE AND CHOOSE THE RIGHT COURSE: stand up and address everyone.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} steps up to address the survivors.

options.text: SITUATION: tell her what the humans are doing to your people.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “They say they don’t wanna take any risks with the deviants… so they’re rounding our people up and taking them to the camps... for extermination. In a few hours, we’re gonna be the only ones left…”

options.text: SURVIVORS: ask her how many of you survived the attack.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “How many of us survived the attack?” {{North}}: “A few hundred? Maybe more if you count those hiding all over the city… If you hadn’t triggered the bomb we’d all be dead.”

options.text: WOUND: ask her about her wound.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “What’s your system status?” {{North}}: “I’m okay… The bullet didn’t hit any biocomponents… You could have been killed trying to save me, {{Markus}}… You have to think of our people first. Nothing else matters.”

options.text: CAMPS: tell her the army has built five camps around the city.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “The army built five different camps in the {{Detroit}} area…” {{North}}: “They’re building more all across the country... They’re preparing for a genocide.”

options.text: HUMBLE: tell her that maybe she was right and you are not the leader your cause needs.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Well, nothing turned out the way I imagined either. Maybe you were right, maybe I’m not the leader our cause needs.”

options.text: FORGIVING: tell her it is too late for regrets; what matters is what you do next.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “It’s too late for regrets now. Our people are dying. What matters now is what we do next…”

options.text: RESENTFUL: tell her she betrayed you when your people needed you most.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You betrayed me! I trusted you, I don’t know how you could turn on me when our people needed me the most!” {{North}}: “I know how you feel, {{Markus}}. You have every right to be angry with me…” {{Markus}}: “You’re goddamn right I do.”

options.text: SITUATION: ask him what the situation is.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “What’s the situation?” {{Simon}}: “They’re taking all our people to camps to be exterminated. In a few hours, we’ll be the only ones left.”

options.text: {{NORTH}}: tell him they killed {{North}} in front of you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “They killed {{North}} right in front of me… And I couldn’t save her…”

options.text: HOW MANY: ask him how many people survived the attack.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “How many people survived the attack?” {{Simon}}: “A few hundred… Maybe more… I don’t know what would have happened if you hadn’t blown up {{Jericho}}…”

options.text: CAMPS: tell him they have built five camps around the city.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “They’ve already built five camps in the {{Detroit}} area alone.” {{Simon}}: “They’re building camps all over the country. They’re organizing our destruction. They’re preparing for a genocide.”

options.text: {{JOSH}}: tell him {{Josh}} died in your arms.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I watched {{Josh}} die in my arms… I should’ve been able to protect him, protect the rest of us and... There was nothing I could do…” {{Simon}}: “{{Josh}} gave his life for the cause. Now, it’s up to us to make sure that he, and the others, didn’t die for nothing.”

adaptationNote: The chart’s [DEVIANTS REGROUP] bracket as a repeatable scene: TALK TO NORTH (with SHARE A MOMENT WITH NORTH), TALK TO KARA, TALK TO JOSH, TALK TO SIMON and TALK TO CONNOR, each once, in any order, each only for someone alive and present; the exit is the string table’s objective FACE YOUR PEOPLE AND CHOOSE THE RIGHT COURSE (MARKUS.CHURCH.SPEECH), which leads to the speech. A talk with its own prompt continues inside this scene with that prompt’s options (option sets 10–13, 20–22, 30–34); TALK TO CONNOR goes to its own scene (M26). Each prompt is one pick (the template records each as a single choice group). Arrows (template, applied once per talk): TALK TO SIMON Simon small up, TALK TO JOSH Josh small up, TALK TO NORTH North small up on both variants, lover or not (the template puts it on the section; the wiki’s “if she is Markus’ lover” is narrower; template wins), HUMBLE a further North small up. North’s talk: if Markus was cast out and fought his way back (`ch30MarkusReturned`, or M22 option 0 before Crossroads is rebuilt), she apologises and the prompt is HUMBLE / FORGIVING / RESENTFUL; otherwise SITUATION / SURVIVORS / WOUND / CAMPS, then her closing line, and at Lover status (built-in `northLover`) “I love you, Markus…” and the chart’s SHARE A MOMENT WITH NORTH (they join hands, wiki North; no arrow of its own; `ch31SharedMoment`). WOUND needs North to have been shot and saved (`ch30NorthWounded`, or M25 option 0; the template is silent, the wiki Notes describe the flag). Simon’s round plays only if North is dead, and JOSH in it only if Josh is dead (template lock); with North alive Simon gives only his closing line. Josh’s talk has no prompt; it adds his line about North if she died. Kara’s talk needs Kara and Alice in the church (alive, not captured, not separated; wiki Markus), has no arrow, and skips the line marked cut (“Well, I hope you make it…”). Lucy never appears (wiki Crossroads).

title: Talk to {{Connor}}
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the church. {{Connor}}, the android who hunted you and who broke from his programming on {{Jericho}}, has just told you: “It’s my fault the humans managed to locate {{Jericho}}… I was stupid… I should’ve guessed they were using me. I’m sorry, {{Markus}}… I can understand if you decide not to trust me…” You must decide if {{Connor}} is trustworthy.

options.text: TRUST: tell him he is one of you now, and his place is with his people.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “You’re one of us, now. Your place is with your people.” {{Connor}}: “There are thousands of androids at the {{CyberLife}} assembly plant. If we could wake them up, they might join us and shift the balance of power…” {{Markus}}: “You wanna infiltrate the {{CyberLife}} Tower? {{Connor}}, that’s suicide…” {{Connor}}: “They trust me, they’ll let me in. If anyone has a chance of infiltrating {{CyberLife}}, it’s me.” {{Markus}}: “If you go there, they will kill you.” {{Connor}}: “There’s a high probability… but statistically speaking, there’s always a chance for unlikely events to take place…” {{Markus}}: “Be careful…”

options.text: DON’T TRUST: tell him your cause is too important to take any risks.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Our cause is too important. I can’t take any risks…” {{Markus}} draws his gun and shoots {{Connor}}.

adaptationNote: The chart’s TALK TO CONNOR and its pair KILL CONNOR / SPARE CONNOR, which are the game’s buttons DON’T TRUST / TRUST (template order: TRUST first); the string table’s objective is DECIDE IF CONNOR IS TRUSTWORTHY. Offered only when a deviant Connor reached the church (built-in `deviant` and `connor`, with the raid) and Markus goes to him. Connor’s plan for the tower is revealed only after TRUST, as in the game, and North does not speak here. TRUST: Jericho small up (template), `ch31ConnorFate` 'spared' (Battle for Detroit: Connor goes to the tower). DON’T TRUST: Markus shoots him (wiki Markus: “pulling out his gun and executing him”); the chart’s A NEW CONNOR WILL BE SENT; Connor is no longer deviant and is replaced; `ch31ConnorFate` 'killed'. No stat change on DON’T TRUST: the template has none; the wiki’s Relationship_Stat lists a Jericho small down, which the reliability log would favour on a death outcome, but the template is followed here and the difference is flagged (open question 3). The pre-rebuild North +1, Josh −1 and the default death arrows (instability, Hank, Amanda) had no source and are gone.

title: The speech
situation: You are {{Markus}}, before your people. You tell them: “Humans have decided to exterminate us… Our people are packed in camps right now, being destroyed… Time has come to make a choice, one that very well may determine the future of our people.”

situationWhen.text: The survivors fill the church in front of you.
Your people fill {{Jericho}}’s hold in front of you.

options.text: DEMONSTRATION: tell them you will demand justice peacefully, without violence.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I know... I know you’re all angry. And I know you wanna fight back... But I assure you violence is not the answer here. We are gonna tell them peacefully that we want justice. If there’s any humanity in them, they will listen. And if not, others will take our place and continue this fight. Are you ready to follow me?” The androids: “{{Markus}}! YEAH! YEAH! YES! YEAH! YES!”

options.text: REVOLUTION: tell them that if humans want war, they will get it.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Now, if they want war... they’ll get it. We are gonna fight for our freedom. And we will succeed or die… Are you ready to follow me?” The androids: “{{Markus}}! YEAH! YEAH! YES! YEAH! YES!”

adaptationNote: The chart’s VIOLENT ATTACK / PEACEFUL PROTEST, which appears under both MARKUS AMONG THE PEOPLE and MARKUS ON SACRED GROUND; the game’s buttons are DEMONSTRATION / REVOLUTION, in the template’s order. No requirement on either (no public-opinion, Jericho or companion gate in any source). Arrows (template, matching the wiki): DEMONSTRATION Josh small up, North small down, Jericho large up; REVOLUTION North small up, Josh small down, Jericho large up; a dead companion’s arrow is not applied. Sets `movement` and `ch31MarkusEnding` (MARKUS CHOSE TO PROTEST FOR HIS PEOPLE / MARKUS CHOSE TO FIGHT FOR HIS PEOPLE, both cross-chapter impacts). REVOLUTION also keeps the pre-rebuild `markusOutcome` = 'liberated' that Battle for Detroit’s scenes still read. The unused string HOSTAGES is not built.
